slides.text: Detective Elias had spent thirty years solving murders. Yet one detail haunted him more than any unsolved case. In every crime scene photograph—stretching back almost eighty years—there was the same man. Sometimes he stood across the street. Sometimes behind a café window. Once, reflected in a puddle. Always watching. Always expressionless. And somehow, never aging.

After months of searching, Elias finally found him sitting alone on a park bench. The man smiled before Elias even spoke. 'You're the first detective to notice me,' he said. 'Most only see the bodies.' Elias demanded answers. 'Were you the killer?' The stranger shook his head gently. 'No. I was the witness. Every single time.'

The man opened a weathered notebook. Every page contained a victim's name, the exact moment they died, and one heartbreaking sentence about the life they could have lived. 'Someone has to remember them,' he whispered. Elias looked up for just a second. The bench was empty. Only the notebook remained—with one blank page waiting at the end.
